title: We launched a supplement brand 3 weeks ago and published a lab report for every ingredient. Here's what it did for trust.
text:
Some context. I worked in corporate for 10+ years and started SILT, a morning and a night drink mix for busy professionals. Before launch we decided to publish everything: the dose of each of the 19 ingredients, the studies, and a lab report for every ingredient. 293 lab checks so far, 0 failed.

What I learned:

People do read them. A pre-booker asked us on Instagram for the exact mg and IU of D3, B12 and K2, and that question only comes from someone who checks.

It shortens the trust gap. We had 1,870 pre-bookings before a single review existed, and the most common question was "how do I know what's inside?"

It's also a discipline on us. Once the reports are public, you can't quietly change a supplier.

With FSSAI tightening nutraceutical labelling and sites like Trustified publishing pass and fail results, I think this becomes table stakes in India within a couple of years.

Founders in consumer brands, what did you make public early that you were nervous about? Did it help or hurt?
